title: The Code Lab & Challenges
summary: Discover where to find your code, what an experiment is, and how to conquer optional challenges.

steps.title: Welcome to the Code Lab
steps.markdownContent:
Once your hardware is built, you need to give it a brain. That's what the **Code Lab** is for.

The Code Lab gives you the exact C++ sketches you need to upload to your Arduino to make your circuit come alive.

quickCheck.question: What is the role of the Code Lab in Monster Lab?
options: To write, review, and test code sketches before uploading to your Arduino
quickCheck.explanation: The Code Lab lets you deconstruct Arduino sketches, understand syntax, and solve programming challenges!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: The Code Lab is where you give your monster circuits their personality and smart behaviors.

quickCheck.question: What should you check when your code has a syntax error?
options: Look for missing semicolons, unmatched parentheses, or typos in command names
quickCheck.explanation: C++ compilers are very precise: missing semicolons or spelling mistakes are the most common syntax errors!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: If a sentence forgets a period, it looks strange. Code needs its semicolons and correct spellings.

steps.title: The IDE Connection
steps.markdownContent:
You don't type code directly into Monster Lab on your phone or tablet to run it. 

Instead, you use a computer running the **Arduino IDE** (Integrated Development Environment). You'll copy the code from the Code Lab, paste it into the IDE on your computer, and click **Upload**.

We'll cover exactly how the IDE works in the next lesson!

steps.title: The Upload Pipeline
steps.markdownContent:
When you click Upload, your code goes on a journey. It gets **Compiled** (translated into machine language) and then sent over the USB cable to the Arduino's memory.

Watch the pipeline simulator below to see how your text becomes a running program!

steps.title: What are Challenges?
steps.markdownContent:
After you finish a lesson's main code, you'll unlock **Challenges**.

Challenges are optional, extra-hard missions where you have to modify the code or the wiring yourself, without step-by-step instructions. They are the best way to earn extra XP and prove you've mastered the concept!

steps.title: Code Lab Review
steps.markdownContent: Let's check your understanding of the Code Lab.

questions.question: Where do you actually upload code to the Arduino?
options: Directly from the Monster Lab app on your phone
From the Arduino IDE on a computer
You don't need to upload code
questions.explanation: You use the Arduino IDE on your computer to compile and upload the sketches.

questions.question: What are Challenges?
options: Optional, extra-hard missions to modify code or wiring
questions.explanation: Challenges are optional missions that test your mastery and give you extra XP.

questions.question: What happens when code is 'compiled'?
options: It is translated from C++ into machine language the Arduino understands
questions.explanation: Compilation turns human-readable code into machine instructions.
